page: The Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-3200s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built for memory-heavy and data-dense enterprise workloads. Driven by an AMD EPYC processor running at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz, the instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by support for instruction sets including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Resource allocation includes 256.0 GB of system memory, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio that aligns directly with memory-optimized architectures. Local persistence is supplied via a integrated 3200 GB NVMe SSD, eliminating external disk latency for local data pipelines. In benchmark evaluations, the memory subsystem demonstrates high throughput, delivering 444.47 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations and 197.86 GB/sec in large-block write operations, both landing within the top 10% tier. The dedicated cores also registered top-tier stress-ng single-core results (3144.58) and strong multi-core throughput exceeding 100,000 points.

Synthetic application tests indicate balanced general compute capabilities alongside strong data processing. The platform scored 71.28 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and demonstrated strong throughput during Clang software compilation and ray tracing. While Geekbench single-core (1867.0) and multi-core (15435.0) scores settle into median tiers due to the 2.0 GHz clock rate, the massive memory capacity and fast uncached memory bandwidth offset raw clock limitations for sustained parallel jobs.

This server provides strong cost efficiency by combining dedicated EPYC execution cores, significant local NVMe storage, and top-tier memory bandwidth in a unified deployment. Without dedicated GPU accelerators, it is engineered for in-memory databases like Redis, caching layers, distributed data engineering pipelines, Clang build farms, and heavy backend transactional databases.
description: The Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-3200s-amd is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by a 2.0 GHz AMD EPYC processor configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores. It features 256.0 GB of system RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside an integrated 3200 GB NVMe SSD for fast local data access. Benchmarks show top-tier uncached memory read bandwidth of 444.47 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 197.86 GB/sec, complemented by strong stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU performance. The instance achieves over 71 million Redis SET operations per second, making it well matched for high-throughput data access. While base clock rates lead to median single-threaded results in Geekbench, the system provides an efficient balance of compute density, local NVMe capacity, and sustained memory throughput. It is specifically designed for in-memory databases, large-scale caching tiers, transactional workloads, and data analysis pipelines.
